liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Fire On The Mountain** (3 reviews): Reviewer was held spellbound by Fire On The Mountain right through to its last notes; Reviewer defends Fire On The Mountain as a terrific song, citing its lyrics and ancient-sounding beat [18][20][24]
- **One More Saturday Night** (1 review): Reviewer saw the Saturday Night into Fire opening pairing as especially wild [21]
- **Cryptical Envelopment** (1 review): Reviewer says Cryptical Envelopment was played for the first time in years [25]
- **Comes A Time** (1 review): Reviewer says Comes A Time was a standout, alongside Fire On The Mountain [24]

## The recordings

- **gd85-07-13.sbd.georges.372.sbefail.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 20 songs; 145 min; rated 4.29/5 by 42 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the soundboard exceptionally clear; Reviewer calls the soundboard quality crystal clear; Reviewer describes the sound as crisp, with strong energy in the playing [1][16][18][19][26]
- **gd1985-07-13.nak300.tonys.77489.sbeok.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 148 min; rated 4.33/5 by 3 [2]. Said about its sound: Recording has prominent 1985 bass thump and the heavy Pacific wind rumble typical of Ventura [2]
- **gd1985-07-13.senn441.mccue.ford.89032.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 21 songs; 148 min; rated 4/5 by 2 [3]. Said about its sound: Distortion, mostly in the second set, comes from a blown amp of Phil's [3]
- **gd1985-07-13.BeyerM160.connor.76913.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 20 songs; 146 min; rated 3/5 by 3 [4]. Said about its sound: Close, up-front sound from the front of the board; static in the second set comes from Phil's bass [4]

## Around the show

- Reviewer mentions photos in The Golden Road showing gusty winds at the show [21]
- Strong wind blew all day, whipping around the stage and causing odd sounds on the soundboard [26]
- Uploader's niece Edris met Bear at this show, and he got her backstage [4]
- Reviewer says the setlist avoids the usual song choices and is unusual compared with typical shows [19]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd85-07-13.sbd.georges.372.sbefail.shnf**: source: SBDmc> DAT> CD> eac> cool edit> shn [1]. Also: Soundboard master cassette to DAT to CD, extracted and edited in Cool Edit, then converted to SHN; via N. Georges [1]
- **gd1985-07-13.nak300.tonys.77489.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Tony Suraci; transferred by Tony Suraci; source: Nakamichi CM301's(split)>Sony D5M Directly behind SBD, one stand at each corner at 10 ft. [2]. Also: Taper applied a mild high-pass filter and adjusted azimuth to reduce wind rumble and high-end wind push; Mics were split because the soundboard was high and directly in front of the taper [2]
- **gd1985-07-13.senn441.mccue.ford.89032.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Adam; transferred by Alex Ford; source: 2 x Sennheiser 441 > Sony D5 > Sony D5 > 2 x Maxell MX 90 [3]. Also: Transferred from master audience cassettes supplied by Mark McCue; 24-bit transfer and editing by Alex Ford, December 2007; Tape flips were patched using a Beyer source [3]
- **gd1985-07-13.BeyerM160.connor.76913.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Jim Vita and Charlie Connor; transferred by Charlie Connor; source: FOB>(Jim Vita's)Beyer Dynamic M160's>Sony TCD5M >Sony TCD5M (Charlie Connor's CM - TDK MA90's) [4]. Also: Recorded with Beyer M160 mics, patched from Jim Vita's spot; seed dedicated to his memory [4]

## Art and photos

- Poster by John Richards Grateful Dead: [1985-07-13 Ventura County Fairgrounds, Ventura, CA, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1985-07-13-ventura-county-fairgrounds-ventura-ca-usa/) [28]
- Poster by Worthpoint: [GratefuL Dead Ventura FairgroundS 1985 FLYer | #4620409115](https://www.worthpoint.com/worthopedia/grateful-dead-ventura-fairgrounds-4620409115) [29]
